1.0.0.en: That which was from the beginning: the eternal Christ.

1.0.1.en: The Word of life: Christ is the Word of God, that is, the divine reason and wisdom. He is called the Word of life because His life is in Himself; He is the origin of life and indeed its source for the whole world.

1.0.2.en: The beloved John was the last of the disciples to live on earth. Here he bears witness to the eternal God who became incarnate in the fullness of time, and whom he saw, heard and touched together with the rest of the disciples and the crowds. He is an eyewitness of the Incarnation of Christ, His teachings and His redemption, and was among those closest to Him. This opening of the epistle gives it strength, since it comes from a trustworthy source, that is, sound teachings received from God, who humbled Himself and became incarnate in order to draw near to us in simplicity, so that we may feel His love and He may lift us up to Himself.

1.1.0.en: Through the Incarnation of Christ we saw the God who is eternal and everlasting, for He is the Life that was from eternity and will be forever. He appeared to us in order to redeem us and give us life by His death for us. Here John clearly bears witness to the divinity of Christ: that He is eternal and everlasting, that He is the source of life for all people, that He was with the Father from eternity, and that He became incarnate in the fullness of time to give blessed eternal life to those who believe in Him. This is the aim of the preaching of John and of all the Apostles.

1.2.0.en: The Apostle declares the purpose of his epistle and of his witness to Christ, which is that we believe in Him, so that we may have fellowship with John, the disciples and all who believe in Christ, who enjoy fellowship with God the Father, known in the Old Testament, and the Son, who revealed Himself in the New Testament, that is, with God in all His hypostases. This fellowship means membership in His Body, that is, the Church, and union with Him by partaking of His Body and Blood.

1.3.0.en: The purpose of the proclamation and of fellowship with God is joy, indeed complete joy, for we are saved from the dominion of sin and death and enjoy a continual relationship with God in this life and forever.

1.3.1.en: Think every day of the love of Christ for you, so that you may speak with Him and enjoy His company, for He alone is the source of life and joy in the world. He is near to you and wants to be united with you in His Holy Sacraments. He dwells in you to stir your longings with love for Him, to embrace your life, comfort your heart and support you in every step.

1.3.2.en: (2) The life of light (vv. 5-7:) 5 "This then is the message which we have heard of him, and declare unto you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all. 6 If we say that we have fellowship with him, and walk in darkness, we lie, and do not the truth: 7 But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin."

1.4.0.en: The message: the teachings of Christ.

1.4.1.en: In his epistle John conveys the teachings of Christ, whose foundation is that God is light, that is, perfectly pure, righteous and good, and that there is no darkness in Him, that is, no sin in Him.

1.5.0.en: He declares that faith in Christ and fellowship with Him are not by words alone but also by deeds. If we are negligent and treat sin as permissible, we are not children of light, for light has no fellowship with darkness, that is, holiness with sin. God is light, so His children are also children of light who walk in righteousness, and if they sin they quickly return through repentance and regain their light.

1.6.0.en: The proof of our sonship to God, who is light, is our walking in a life of light, and this will place us in pure fellowship of love with those around us. Our means of obtaining the life of light is to be cleansed by the blood of Christ the Redeemer through the Sacraments of the Church.

1.6.1.en: When the light of dawn and of the new day shines upon you, remember that you are a child of light because God is light. Then you will walk in purity, and if you fall you will repent quickly and take care to do every positive deed that establishes you in the life of light.

1.7.0.en: The believer is liable to fall into sin, but his repentance and confession remove it from him by the blood of Christ in the Sacrament of Repentance and Confession. Let no one be proud and say that he has no sin, for this is a kind of self-deception and an attempt to deceive others; indeed it is a new sin called self-justification and unrepentance. Persistence in unrepentance is error and distance from the truth, and it leads in the end to perdition.

1.8.0.en: The mercy and love of God appear in the forgiveness of the sins of everyone who repents. He is faithful in His promises of mercy to the repentant, and at the same time just, since He lifts our sins from us to His Cross, on which He bore all our sins and died to redeem us, and so paid our debt for us. Thus mercy is united with justice in Christ the Redeemer, and we receive His mercy in the Sacrament of Confession.

1.9.0.en: Whoever does not confess his sins not only deprives himself of God's forgiveness, goes astray and departs from the truth, but also ascribes falsehood to God. For Christ was crucified to take away the sins of mankind, so this person's claim that he has no sin makes the redemption of Christ needless and turns God's call to us to repent into false words. This misguided person also declares his own unrepentance and that the word of God has no place in him, for he refuses to hear it so as to repent.

1.9.1.en: May you enjoy God's mercy and forgiveness by hastening to repent through prayer, through examining yourself, and before your father of confession, for God loves the weak but hates the proud.

1.9.2.en: Faith and love for the brethren

2.0.s.en: (1) Christ the Advocate and abiding in Him

2.0.0.en: St. John's words about the life of light in Christ and about holiness are meant to keep his children from falling into sin. But as human beings we are liable to it, and no one is without sin, so he offers us the solution, who is Christ the Redeemer. He intercedes for us by His blood on the Cross and is ready to forgive our sins as long as we repent of them, because He is righteous and holy, without sin. He died for us and intercedes for us by His blood before divine justice, asking forgiveness for everyone among those who believe in Him who repents.

2.1.0.en: The blood of Christ is sufficient to atone for the sins of all people if they believe in Him and repent. Because it is unlimited, His atonement is unlimited, forgiving the sins of those who believe in Him in the Church and of all who will believe in Him throughout the ages and in every place.

2.2.0.en: In Christianity the knowledge of God is not theoretical knowledge but practical, by carrying out His commandments. One who loves someone strives to carry out his word, and even if the commandment seems heavy, whoever loves God accepts it with contentment and joy in order to please Him.

2.3.0.en: Whoever claims to know God, knowing some theoretical matters about Him, while refusing or neglecting to carry out His commandments, deceives himself, and God does not dwell in him. For if he loved God and were united with the Truth, who is Christ, by partaking of His Body and Blood, he would surely strive to carry out His commandments.

2.4.0.en: A person's love for God is in proportion to his carrying out of God's word, and whoever keeps all His word becomes perfect in love. Whoever loves God becomes steadfast in Him, and this is indeed a proof of God's dwelling in him.

2.5.0.en: The Apostle affirms, from another side, that the proof of abiding in Christ is to follow Him in love, for in Christ the perfection of love appears in complete self-giving even to death on the Cross. So whoever loves God carries out His commandments, whatever he must give, even unto death.

2.5.1.en: Reject your sin however sweet its pleasure seems or however much you incline to it. Reject sin however small it is, and draw near to God with all your strength; then your love for Him will be shown and His mercies will overflow upon you.

2.6.0.en: As the beloved John speaks about love, he declares that it is not a new commandment for mankind but old, from the creation of man. Adam loved his wife because she was part of him, and Cain was troubled by his lack of love for his brother and killed him; so it has been with all mankind, until the Ten Commandments proclaimed this love in the last six commandments, by honoring others and not wronging them.

2.7.0.en: Love is considered a new commandment in Christianity in two respects:

2.7.1.en: 1- The appearance of new depths in it, in love even to death on the Cross.

2.7.2.en: 2- The possibility of carrying out this deep love by the power of the Holy Spirit who dwells in the believers. God is love and truth, so love is the perfect truth in God which works in us. It is also the proof of the life of light, or rather it is the light that entered into us through Christ, the Light of the world, who laid down His life for us. When the light dwells in us, darkness withdraws, that is, sin, which includes selfishness, hatred and wronging others.

2.8.0.en: If anyone does not love his brethren among men, but is annoyed with them and hates them, let him not claim that he knows God, the true Light, for he is surely still in the darkness of sin and error.

2.9.0.en: Love for the brethren is the proof of our love for God and of abiding in Him, so that we become people of light like Him, attract others to love, and do not cause anyone to stumble or turn away from Him, because we have kept away from hatred and wronging others.

2.10.0.en: Whoever rejects love and sinks into his selfishness, being annoyed with others and persisting in that, has fallen into the darkness of sin and turned away from God, and advances from error to error even if his thoughts seem logical to himself.

2.10.1.en: Beware of the provocations of Satan against you that make you annoyed with the actions of others. Know that they need your love, so pray for them and yield as much as you can to show your love for them. By this you abide in God, enjoy His peace and blessings, and draw others to Him as far as they respond to Him.

2.11.0.en: He speaks about the details of applying love at different ages, beginning with the little children who received the grace of Baptism, so that their nature became pure, inclined to love God and others, and their ancestral sin was forgiven. By "children" he may mean all the members of the Church, because they are his children who have enjoyed the grace of Baptism and the forgiveness of their sins and live by love within the Church.

2.12.0.en: He addresses this epistle to all ages:

2.12.1.en: Fathers, because you have known him that is from the beginning: By fathers he means the elderly and the priests, because through their many years they have experienced the love of God who is from the beginning, which calls them to walk in love toward all. Young men, because you have overcome the wicked one: By young men are meant the youth, distinguished by strength, activity and burning love, by which they overcome the devil, the wicked one, who stirs up disturbances, troubles and hatred among people.

2.12.2.en: Little children, because you have known the Father: By children he means either the little ones or the whole Church, his children, and he reminds them that they have known the love of God the Father, who gave His beloved Son for our redemption, and have enjoyed His care, and so they hold fast to love in their conduct with those around them.

2.13.0.en: He reaffirms the meanings mentioned in the preceding two verses, whether for the elderly or the young, declaring that in his epistle here and in his words about love he confirms what he had also written before in his Gospel about this love.

2.13.1.en: Love is your strong weapon against the wars of the devil, so be careful to forgive however great the faults of others, and indeed offer words and deeds of love as much as you can; then you will protect yourself and those around you from the arrows of the devil.

2.14.0.en: Since the Apostle speaks about the love of God, from which love for the brethren results, he warns us of its chief obstacle, which is love of the world, by which he means the material things in it and attachment to them. The heart either loves God or the world, so Christ calls us to love with all the heart when He says, "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart" (Lk 10:27).

2.15.0.en: He explains to us in detail the love of the world, which is summed up as follows:

2.15.1.en: The lust of the flesh: This includes all material desires with all the deviations from the commandment that they bring, as well as excessive concern for the necessary needs of the body. It points to the first temptation of Christ on the mountain, that is, turning stones into bread because He was hungry after forty days of fasting.

2.15.2.en: The lust of the eyes: This is the desire for various material things, positions and outward show, with all the pride they carry within them. It is the second temptation of Christ, in which Satan asked Him to throw Himself down from the pinnacle of the Temple, to descend in a grand manner among the gathered crowds while the angels bore Him up, and this of course carries the meaning of showiness and pride.

2.15.3.en: The pride of life: The inclination to possess and to raise one's material standard, and it is the third temptation, in which Satan tried to entice Christ with the possession of the kingdoms of the world.

2.15.4.en: These various desires naturally have no relation to the love of God but are against it, because they distract us from Him.

2.16.0.en: He warns us that all the desires of the world will come to an end and have no place in eternity, but what remains is the love of God, for it lasts with us forever, and our attachment to His love makes us do His will, so that we find the salvation of our souls.

2.16.1.en: When any material desire draws you, remember that it is temporary and will quickly pass away, so that you draw back from it.

2.16.2.en: And when you use material things, use them in moderation so that your heart is not attached to them, and at the same time try to grow in your prayers and readings, so that you exchange the love of the world for the love of God and enjoy His company forever.

2.17.s.en: (5) The heretics and standing firm before them

2.17.0.en: The last hour: The time between the coming of Christ in the flesh and His Second Coming. It is considered the last because it is the last opportunity for repentance, after Christ has proclaimed His redemption and all the truths of the faith, so that we may seize the opportunity of our lifetime to believe and repent.

2.17.1.en: Antichrists: Those who deny His divinity and teach teachings contrary to His commandments in order to lead people astray. St. John speaks to his believing children to warn them against the heretics who appear at the end of the days as a sign of the approach of the Second Coming, which Christ mentioned in His words about the end of the world (Mt 24:24).

2.18.0.en: These heretics were members of the Church and had the name of Christians, but they did not have the right faith. Before God they were not members of the Church because their thought and heart had turned aside to evil, and because their inner being was not upright they could not remain in the Church and submit to its teachings, so they split from it with their heresies that deny the divinity of Christ.

2.19.0.en: He encourages the believers that the Holy Spirit who dwells in them through the anointing of the Myron which they received from the Holy One guides them and establishes them in the right faith, and uncovers before them the error of the heretics, so that they do not follow them but obey the teachings of the Holy Spirit through the mouths of the Fathers of the Church and its guides, and these heresies do not affect them.

2.20.0.en: He declares to the believers that he affirms and strengthens their faith in Christ, who is the Truth, and that also by the Holy Spirit who dwells in them they know that the words of the heretics are false, because they are against Christ and the teachings they learned in the Church.

2.21.0.en: He exposes the heretics and their false thoughts, because they deny the divinity of Christ and in this way deny God the Father also, for it is He who sent His only begotten Son into the world to reveal Himself visibly to people through Him, "No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him" (Jn 1:18).

2.22.0.en: Christ the Son is the image and substance of the Father, so whoever denies His divinity also denies God the Father, and whoever accepts Him accepts God the Father also.

2.23.0.en: The Apostle urges them to hold fast to the faith which was preached to them and in which they believed, so that they do not turn to the heresies opposed to their faith. Abiding in the faith means abiding in God and enjoying His work in them.

2.24.0.en: By abiding in the faith we receive God's promise of eternal life with Him.

2.25.0.en: Here he makes clear the purpose of the epistle, which is to warn against the heretics who lead them astray from the faith.

2.26.0.en: He reminds them of the Holy Spirit who dwells in them through the anointing of the Sacrament of the Myron, which taught them the faith, helped them to abide in it, and gave them all they need of knowledge about Christ. So they do not need new, strange, false teachings like those the heretics promote, because the anointing of the Holy Spirit is truth and teaches them the truth and not falsehood like these heretics.

2.27.0.en: He calls on them to abide in the faith so that they may enjoy eternal life when He comes in His Second Coming, and not be ashamed on that day because of their turning aside after the teachings of the heretics.

2.28.0.en: The proof of their abiding in faith in Christ, the Righteous and Holy One, is that they live in righteousness, goodness and doing good to others, for by this they are children of God.

2.28.1.en: Do not accept any teachings foreign to what you learned in the Church, however dazzling, even if they reach you from those closest to you. Rather, take refuge in prayer and in your father of confession so that you abide in what you learned and a blessed eternal life awaits you.

2.28.2.en: The characteristics of the children of God
